verses.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
verses.memoryHint: The very first verse of the Bible.

verses.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
verses.memoryHint: God's command to Joshua before entering Canaan.

verses.text: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
verses.memoryHint: A verse of strength and confidence.

verses.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
verses.memoryHint: About God's good purpose in all things.

verses.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
verses.memoryHint: From the Sermon on the Mount.

verses.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
verses.memoryHint: About the guidance of God's word.

verses.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up.
verses.memoryHint: The beginning of the love chapter.

verses.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.
verses.memoryHint: The fruit of the Spirit list.

verses.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
verses.memoryHint: About working with a good heart.

verses.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

characters.name: Noah
clues: I built something huge at God's command.
Animals came to me two by two.
I survived a flood that covered the whole earth.

characters.name: Moses
clues: I was found in a basket among the reeds.
I saw a bush that burned but was not consumed.
I led God's people out of slavery in Egypt.

characters.name: David
clues: I was the youngest of my brothers.
I defeated a giant with a sling and a stone.
I became the second king of Israel.

characters.name: Esther
clues: I became queen of Persia without revealing where I was from.
My cousin raised me after my parents died.
I risked my life to save my people from a plot to destroy them.

characters.name: Daniel
clues: I was taken captive to Babylon as a young man.
I interpreted dreams for a powerful king.
I was thrown into a den of lions for praying.

characters.name: Mary
clues: An angel visited me with surprising news.
I gave birth in a stable in Bethlehem.
I raised a son who would save the world.

characters.name: Peter
clues: I was a fisherman before I was called.
I once tried to walk on water.
I denied knowing my teacher three times.

characters.name: Paul
clues: I once persecuted followers of Jesus.
A bright light blinded me on a journey.
I wrote many letters found in the New Testament.

characters.name: Ruth
clues: I was not born an Israelite.
I refused to leave my mother-in-law.
I became an ancestor of King David.

characters.name: Samson
clues: I was set apart before I was born.
My strength was tied to my uncut hair.
I pushed down the pillars of a temple in my final act.

characters.name: Solomon
clues: My father was King David.
God gave me great wisdom when I asked for it.
I built the first Temple in Jerusalem.

characters.name: Abraham
clues: God called me to leave my homeland for a land I had never seen.
I am called the father of many nations.
I was willing to sacrifice my son Isaac in obedience to God.

characters.name: Joseph
clues: My brothers sold me into slavery out of jealousy.
I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams about famine.
I forgave my brothers and saved my family from starvation.

characters.name: Elijah
clues: I challenged 450 prophets of a false god on a mountain.
Ravens brought me food beside a brook.
I was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

characters.name: Gideon
clues: An angel called me a mighty man of valor while I hid from enemies.
I tested God with a fleece of wool.
I defeated a huge army with just 300 men.

characters.name: Deborah
clues: I was a judge and prophetess who led Israel.
I sat under a palm tree to settle disputes.
I helped lead Israel to victory over a Canaanite army.

characters.name: Nehemiah
clues: I served as cupbearer to a Persian king.
I asked permission to rebuild the walls of my home city.
I rebuilt Jerusalem's walls in fifty-two days despite opposition.

characters.name: Job
clues: I lost my wealth, children, and health in a single trial.
My friends came to comfort me but argued instead.
God restored double what I had lost after my time of testing.

characters.name: Jonathan
clues: I was the son of the first king of Israel.
I made a covenant of friendship with a future king.
I gave my armor and weapons to my closest friend, David.

characters.name: John the Baptist
clues: I lived in the wilderness and ate locusts and wild honey.
I baptized people in the Jordan River.
I told people to prepare the way for the one coming after me.

characters.name: Adam
clues: God formed me from the dust of the ground.
God breathed the breath of life into me, and I became a living soul.
I named all the animals and later ate forbidden fruit in a garden.

characters.name: Eve
clues: I was formed from a rib taken from the first man.
I am called the mother of all living.
A serpent deceived me into eating fruit from a forbidden tree.

characters.name: Sarah
clues: I was married to a man God called out of his homeland.
God promised I would become the mother of nations.
I laughed when I heard I would have a son in my old age.

characters.name: Isaac
clues: My birth was promised to my parents when they were very old.
My father once took me up a mountain to offer me as a sacrifice.
God provided a ram in my place, and I became father to twin sons.

characters.name: Jacob
clues: I was born grasping my twin brother's heel.
I wrestled with a stranger all night and would not let go.
God renamed me Israel, and I became the father of twelve sons.

characters.name: Aaron
clues: I am the older brother of a great leader of Israel.
I spoke to Pharaoh on my brother's behalf.
I became the first high priest of Israel.

characters.name: Miriam
clues: I watched over my baby brother as he floated in a basket on the river.
I am called a prophetess.
I led the women of Israel in song and dance after crossing the sea.

characters.name: Joshua
clues: I served as an assistant to a great leader of Israel.
I was one of only two spies who trusted God's promise about the land.
I led Israel into the promised land after the walls of a city fell.

characters.name: Saul
clues: I was anointed the very first king of Israel.
I stood a head taller than anyone else in Israel.
I grew jealous of a young shepherd who later became king in my place.

characters.name: Samuel
clues: As a boy, I heard God call my name in the night.
I served as the last judge of Israel and a prophet.
I anointed both the first and second kings of Israel.

characters.name: Naomi
clues: I lost my husband and both my sons while living in a foreign land.
I told my daughters-in-law to return to their own people, but one refused to leave me.
I became grandmother to the ancestor of King David.

characters.name: Boaz
clues: I owned fields of barley near Bethlehem.
I noticed a loyal foreign woman gleaning grain behind my workers.
I redeemed and married her, and became an ancestor of King David.

characters.name: Delilah
clues: I lived in the valley of Sorek.
Philistine rulers paid me to discover the secret of a strong man's power.
I cut his hair while he slept, and his strength left him.

characters.name: Nathan
clues: I served as a prophet during the reign of Israel's second king.
I told the king a story about a rich man and a poor man's only lamb.
I confronted the king face to face after his sin with another man's wife.

characters.name: Ezekiel
clues: I was a prophet taken into exile in Babylon.
God showed me a valley full of dry bones.
I prophesied and watched the bones come together and live again.

characters.name: Hosea
clues: I am a prophet whose own marriage became a living picture of God's message.
God told me to marry a woman who would be unfaithful to me.
My story illustrates God's faithful love for an unfaithful people.

characters.name: Thomas
clues: I was one of the twelve apostles.
I was not present the first time the risen Lord appeared to the others.
I said I would not believe until I touched His wounds myself.

characters.name: Andrew
clues: I was a fisherman before I was called to follow Jesus.
I am the brother of a more well-known apostle.
I was the one who first brought my brother to meet Jesus.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
clues: I was one of the twelve chosen to follow Jesus.
I agreed to hand my teacher over for thirty pieces of silver.
I identified Jesus to the soldiers with a kiss.

characters.name: Barnabas
clues: My name means 'son of encouragement.'
I vouched for a former persecutor of the church when others were afraid of him.
I traveled with Paul on his first missionary journey.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene
clues: Jesus freed me from seven demons.
I followed Jesus and supported His ministry.
I was the first to see Him alive after His resurrection.

characters.name: Lazarus
clues: I lived in Bethany with my two sisters.
I fell sick and died while Jesus delayed His visit.
Jesus called me out of the tomb four days after I was buried.

characters.name: Nicodemus
clues: I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
I came to Jesus by night with questions.
I was told that a man must be born again to see the kingdom of God.

characters.name: Zacchaeus
clues: I was a wealthy chief tax collector.
I was too short to see over the crowd, so I climbed a tree.
Jesus invited Himself to my house, and I gave half my goods to the poor.

characters.name: Martha
clues: I welcomed Jesus into my home in Bethany.
I was busy preparing a meal while my sister sat listening to Jesus.
My brother Lazarus was raised from the dead.

characters.name: Simeon
clues: I was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
I was told I would not die until I saw the Lord's Christ.
I took the infant Jesus in my arms in the Temple and blessed God.

characters.name: Pontius Pilate
clues: I was the Roman governor of Judea.
I found no fault in the man brought before me, yet the crowd demanded His death.
I washed my hands before the crowd and delivered Jesus to be crucified.

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathea
clues: I was a rich man and a member of the Jewish council.
I secretly believed in Jesus as His disciple.
I asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in my own new tomb.

characters.name: Pharaoh
clues: I ruled over the greatest empire the Israelites knew.
I hardened my heart again and again as plagues struck my land.
I finally let God's people go after my firstborn son died.

characters.name: Jethro
clues: I was a priest of Midian.
A fugitive shepherd married my daughter and worked for me for years.
I advised my son-in-law to appoint judges to help him lead Israel.

characters.name: Caleb
clues: I was one of the twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
Unlike ten of the others, I believed God could give us the land.
Because I followed the Lord fully, I was allowed to enter the promised land.

characters.name: Balaam
clues: A foreign king hired me to curse the people of Israel.
My donkey saw an angel in the road before I did.
I opened my mouth to curse Israel, but blessings came out instead.

characters.name: Korah
clues: I was a Levite who rose up against Israel's appointed leaders.
I gathered others to challenge the authority God had given.
The ground opened up and swallowed me and my followers.

characters.name: Rahab
clues: I lived in a house built into the city wall of Jericho.
I hid two Israelite spies and helped them escape.
A scarlet cord in my window marked my household to be spared.

characters.name: Isaiah
clues: I saw the Lord high and lifted up, with seraphim calling 'Holy, holy, holy.'
A coal from the altar touched my lips to cleanse me.
I prophesied of a virgin bearing a son called Immanuel.

characters.name: Jeremiah
clues: God told me He knew me before I was formed in the womb.
I am often called the weeping prophet.
I warned Judah of coming judgment and watched Jerusalem fall.

characters.name: Elisha
clues: I poured water on the hands of the prophet before me.
I asked for a double portion of his spirit.
I watched my master taken up to heaven in a whirlwind and took up his mantle.

characters.name: Jonah
clues: God told me to preach against a wicked city, but I ran the other way.
A great fish swallowed me after I was thrown overboard.
I was angry when the people repented and God spared the city.

characters.name: Amos
clues: I was a shepherd before God called me to prophesy.
I preached about justice rolling down like waters.
I warned Israel about the coming Day of the Lord.

characters.name: Micah
clues: I prophesied during the reigns of several kings of Judah.
I named the little town where a ruler over Israel would be born.
I asked what the Lord requires: to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

characters.name: Zechariah
clues: I prophesied after the exiles returned to Jerusalem.
I saw visions to encourage the rebuilding of the Temple.
I foretold a king coming to Jerusalem, lowly, and riding on a donkey.

characters.name: Malachi
clues: My name means 'my messenger.'
I wrote the last book of the Old Testament.
I prophesied that a messenger would come to prepare the way before the Lord.

characters.name: James
clues: I was a fisherman, the son of Zebedee.
Jesus called my brother and me 'Sons of Thunder.'
I was the first of the twelve apostles to be martyred.

characters.name: John
clues: I was a fisherman before Jesus called me.
I am often called the disciple whom Jesus loved.
I wrote a Gospel and was given a vision on the island of Patmos.

characters.name: Philip
clues: I was from Bethsaida, the same town as Peter and Andrew.
Jesus found me and said, 'Follow me.'
I brought my friend Nathanael to meet Jesus.

characters.name: Bartholomew
clues: I am also called Nathanael in one of the Gospels.
I doubted anything good could come from Nazareth.
Jesus called me a true Israelite in whom there was no deceit.

characters.name: Matthew
clues: I collected taxes for Rome before I was called.
Jesus said 'Follow me' as I sat at my tax booth.
I wrote one of the four Gospels.

characters.name: Silas
clues: I was a leader among the early believers in Jerusalem.
I traveled with Paul on his second missionary journey.
I was beaten and imprisoned with Paul, and we sang hymns at midnight.

characters.name: Timothy
clues: My mother and grandmother taught me the Scriptures from childhood.
Paul called me his true son in the faith.
Paul wrote two New Testament letters directly to me.

characters.name: Mark
clues: I am also called John Mark.
I traveled with Paul and Barnabas, then later with Peter.
I wrote one of the four Gospels.

events.text: God tells Noah to build an ark because a flood is coming.
Noah builds the ark and gathers two of every kind of animal.
The flood covers the whole earth for forty days and nights.
Noah sends out a raven and then a dove to find dry land.
God sets a rainbow in the sky as a promise never to flood the earth again.
Moses is called by God at the burning bush.
Moses asks Pharaoh to let God's people go.
God sends ten plagues on Egypt.
The Israelites eat the Passover meal and leave Egypt.
God parts the Red Sea so Israel can cross on dry ground.
The Israelites receive the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai.
The Philistine army gathers to fight Israel, led by the giant Goliath.
David visits his brothers at the battle camp.
David volunteers to fight Goliath, trusting in God.
David defeats Goliath with a sling and a stone.
The Philistine army flees, and Israel celebrates the victory.
The angel Gabriel tells Mary she will give birth to Jesus.
Mary and Joseph travel to Bethlehem for a census.
Jesus is born and laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn.
Shepherds visit after angels announce the good news to them.
Wise men from the East follow a star to worship the newborn king.
Jesus shares the Last Supper with His disciples.
Jesus is betrayed by Judas and arrested in the garden.
Jesus is crucified on a cross at Golgotha.
Jesus is buried in a tomb, and a stone seals the entrance.
Jesus rises from the dead on the third day.
Jesus appears to His disciples before ascending to heaven.
People settle in Shinar and decide to build a city and a tower to the heavens.
They begin building with brick and tar to make a name for themselves.
God comes down to see the tower the people are building.
God confuses their language so they can no longer understand one another.
The people scatter across the earth, and the city is called Babel.
God calls Abraham to leave his home for a land God will show him.
God promises Abraham he will become the father of many nations.
God tests Abraham by asking him to sacrifice his son Isaac.
Abraham obeys and travels to Mount Moriah to offer Isaac.
God provides a ram and stops Abraham at the last moment.
Joseph's brothers become jealous of him and sell him into slavery.
Joseph is taken to Egypt and put in charge of Potiphar's house.
Joseph is falsely accused and thrown into prison.
Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is made second in command over Egypt.
Joseph's brothers come to Egypt for food, and Joseph forgives and reveals himself to them.
Moses asks Pharaoh to let the Israelites go, but Pharaoh refuses.
God sends plagues of blood, frogs, and gnats upon Egypt.
God sends more plagues, including flies, livestock disease, boils, hail, locusts, and darkness.
The final plague brings death to every firstborn in Egypt.
Pharaoh finally lets the Israelites leave after the tenth plague.
Pharaoh changes his mind and chases the Israelites with his army.
The Israelites are trapped between Pharaoh's army and the Red Sea.
Moses stretches out his hand, and God parts the sea.
The Israelites cross on dry ground with walls of water on each side.
The sea closes over Pharaoh's army as they try to follow.

stories.title: Joshua and the Battle of Jericho

events.text: Joshua sends spies into Jericho, who are helped by Rahab.
God tells Joshua to march around the city once a day for six days.
On the seventh day, the priests and army march around the city seven times.
The priests blow their trumpets, and the people give a great shout.
The walls of Jericho fall down, and Israel takes the city.
God tells the prophet Samuel that He has chosen a new king from the sons of Jesse.
Samuel looks at Jesse's older sons, but God says He does not judge by outward appearance.
Jesse brings his youngest son David in from tending the sheep.
Samuel anoints David with oil in front of his brothers.
The Spirit of the Lord comes powerfully upon David from that day on.

stories.title: Elijah and the Prophets of Baal

events.text: King Ahab and the prophets of Baal challenge Elijah on Mount Carmel.
The prophets of Baal cry out to their god all day, but nothing happens.
Elijah rebuilds an altar to the Lord and has it soaked with water.
Elijah prays, and fire falls from heaven, consuming the sacrifice.
The people see the fire and declare that the Lord is God.
Daniel continues to pray to God three times a day despite a new law.
Daniel's enemies trick the king into signing a law against prayer.
Daniel is caught praying and thrown into the den of lions.
God sends an angel to shut the mouths of the lions overnight.
The king finds Daniel unharmed the next morning and praises God.
God tells Jonah to go preach to the city of Nineveh.
Jonah runs away and boards a ship sailing the opposite direction.
A great storm arises, and the sailors throw Jonah into the sea.
A great fish swallows Jonah, and he prays to God from inside it.
The fish spits Jonah onto dry land, and he goes to preach in Nineveh.
Esther becomes queen of Persia without revealing that she is Jewish.
Haman plots to destroy all the Jewish people in the kingdom.
Mordecai asks Esther to approach the king on behalf of her people.
Esther risks her life by appearing before the king uninvited.
The king grants Esther's request, and her people are saved.
Jesus goes up on a mountainside, and His disciples come to Him.
Jesus teaches the Beatitudes, blessing the poor in spirit and the meek.
Jesus teaches about being salt and light in the world.
Jesus teaches His followers how to pray using the Lord's Prayer.
Jesus concludes by teaching about building a house on the rock.
A large crowd follows Jesus to a remote place to hear Him teach.
Evening comes, and the disciples want to send the hungry crowd away.
A boy offers five loaves and two fish to Jesus.
Jesus gives thanks and breaks the bread, and it multiplies to feed everyone.
Twelve baskets of leftovers are gathered after everyone eats.
A younger son asks his father for his inheritance early and leaves home.
The son wastes his wealth in wild living in a distant country.
A severe famine hits, and the son ends up feeding pigs, starving.
The son comes to his senses and decides to return home to his father.
The father runs to meet his son, forgives him, and celebrates his return.

stories.title: Paul's Conversion on the Road to Damascus

events.text: Saul travels toward Damascus intending to arrest followers of Jesus.
A bright light from heaven suddenly shines around him.
Saul hears the voice of Jesus asking why he is persecuting Him.
Saul is blinded and led into the city, where he fasts for three days.
Ananias visits Saul, his sight is restored, and he is baptized.
